description: Turn repositories into Jupyter-enabled Docker images

summary.one_liner: repo2docker fetches a git repository and builds a Docker image from configuration files found inside it, optionally launching a Jupyter-enabled container to explore the contents.
summary.what_it_does: It takes a git repository (from GitHub or a local path) and builds a container image based on the configuration files in that repository. The build is driven by files the repo contains, and the README points to a list of supported configuration files in the documentation. Optionally it launches the built container so you can explore the repository, which the README describes as a Jupyter Notebook with the repository contents. On startup it prints a URL with a login token to paste into a browser. It is installed as a Python package and run from the command line. The README says Docker must be running on the machine for it to work. The project is inspired by Heroku Build Packs, per the README.
use_cases: turn a git repository into a reproducible Docker image
launch a Jupyter notebook environment from a GitHub repo
build containers for Binder-style shared research environments
run a local repository inside a Jupyter container
package a project's dependencies as a container image
notable: Builds images from configuration files already in the repository rather than requiring a separate Dockerfile
Can fetch repositories from GitHub or from a local path
Can run inside a Docker container when given access to the Docker daemon, as used by BinderHub
Images published to quay.io; the old Docker Hub image is no longer supported
caveats: Supported on Linux and macOS; Windows support is described only in the documentation
